name: Bilbo's Journey
description: There and back again at real scale: about 1,850 miles (≈3,000 km) from Bag End to the Lonely Mountain and home, an estimate from the maps; exact figures vary. Heights are invented.

bag-end.name: Bag End
bag-end.text: Thirteen dwarves, one wizard and far too many dishes. Bilbo runs out without a handkerchief.

trollshaws.name: The Trollshaws
trollshaws.text: Three trolls argue over how to cook dwarves until the sun comes up.

rivendell.name: Rivendell
rivendell.text: A rest, a good supper and moon-letters read on an old map.

misty-mountains.name: The Misty Mountains
misty-mountains.text: Stone giants toss rocks in the storm. You shelter in a cave that isn't empty.

goblin-town.name: Goblin-town
goblin-town.text: Tunnels, drums and a very angry Great Goblin.

gollum-lake.name: The Underground Lake
gollum-lake.text: A game of riddles in the dark, and a ring found on the tunnel floor.

eagles-eyrie.name: The Eagles' Eyrie
eagles-eyrie.text: Wolves below, fire in the trees, and then great wings.

beorn.name: Beorn's House
beorn.text: Honey, cream and a host who is sometimes a bear.

mirkwood.name: Mirkwood
mirkwood.text: Don't leave the path. Everybody leaves the path.

elvenking-halls.name: The Elvenking's Halls
elvenking-halls.text: The dwarves are locked up. Bilbo, invisible, finds the keys.

forest-river.name: The Forest River
forest-river.text: Out of the cellars in barrels, bumping down the river.

lake-town.name: Lake-town
lake-town.text: A town on stilts cheers for the King under the Mountain.

lonely-mountain.name: The Lonely Mountain
lonely-mountain.text: A secret door, a sleeping dragon, and more gold than anyone can count.

beorn-return.name: Yule at Beorn's
beorn-return.text: The way home starts slowly: a long rest by Beorn's fire.

rivendell-return.name: Rivendell Again
rivendell-return.text: Songs and a soft bed on the way home.

home-again.name: Home Again
home-again.text: Your furniture is being auctioned. You buy most of it back.

story.contract: A contract for a burglar, with a share of the treasure and funeral costs covered.
story.ponies: Rain, ponies and no second breakfast.
story.dark-forest: Weeks under the trees. Food runs low and nobody has seen the sun.
story.arkenstone: Armies gather at the mountain, and Bilbo makes a brave, difficult choice.
story.homeward: The way home is quiet. You are not the same hobbit who left.

facts.exam-paper: Tolkien wrote the book's famous first sentence on a blank page of a student's exam paper while marking.
facts.rayner: Before publishing, Stanley Unwin paid his ten-year-old son Rayner a shilling to review the manuscript. Rayner liked it.
facts.published: The Hobbit was published on 21 September 1937, with illustrations and a dust jacket designed by Tolkien himself.
facts.dwarf-names: The dwarves' names, and Gandalf's, come from a list of dwarves in the Old Norse poem Völuspá.
facts.gollum-rewrite: In the first edition Gollum was ready to give up his ring. Tolkien rewrote the chapter in 1951 to fit The Lord of the Rings.
facts.beorn-name: Beorn's name means "man" or "warrior" in Old English and is related to the Old Norse word for bear.
facts.mirkwood-name: Mirkwood is an old name: a dark forest called Myrkviðr appears in Norse legends.
facts.smaug-name: Tolkien called the dragon's name a low philological joke, from an old Germanic verb meaning to squeeze through a hole.
facts.duration: By the book's calendar the adventure took more than a year: Bilbo left in spring and came home the next summer.
facts.sales: The Hobbit has sold over 100 million copies and has been translated into dozens of languages, Ukrainian among them.

dangers.troll-fire: Firelight in the woods, and big voices arguing about dinner.
dangers.goblins: The cave floor opens in the night and goblins pour out.
dangers.wargs: Wolves gather in a clearing below, and goblins set the trees alight.
dangers.spiders: Webs across the path, and many eyes in the dark.
dangers.dragon-wakes: The dragon wakes. The whole mountain shakes with its anger.
dangers.five-armies: Five armies meet beneath the mountain.

big-day.name: Long Day on the Road
big-day.description: Walk 25 km in a single day.
